title: Quick tip: the ten-minute check-in.
hook: Quick tip: the ten-minute check-in.
caption:
Quick tip: the ten-minute check-in.
Once a week, sit down together for ten minutes. Two questions: "What felt heavy this week?" and "What's one thing that would make next week lighter?"
Phones away, no fixing, just listening. Ten minutes is doable. Try it this Sunday.

Much Love
Emma x

title: ONE BAD MEAL DIDN’T RUIN YOUR PROGRESS.
hook: ONE BAD MEAL DIDN’T RUIN YOUR PROGRESS.
caption:
ONE BAD MEAL DIDN’T RUIN YOUR PROGRESS.

And one healthy meal didn’t create it either.

Too many people eat one higher-calorie meal, see the scale jump the next morning, and immediately think they’ve ruined weeks of hard work.

But here’s what you need to understand. 👇

⚖️ The scale doesn’t just measure body fat.

After a larger meal, your weight may increase because of:
💧 Temporary water retention
🍚 Increased glycogen storage
🧂 Higher sodium intake
🍽️ More food sitting in your digestive system

That doesn’t automatically mean you’ve gained body fat.

title: DISCIPLINE GETS QUIETER OVER TIME
hook: DISCIPLINE GETS QUIETER OVER TIME
caption:
DISCIPLINE GETS QUIETER OVER TIME

When you first start trying to become consistent, everything can feel like a battle.

Getting out of bed.
Going to the gym.
Preparing your food.
Choosing training instead of staying home.

You keep waiting for the day when you suddenly become incredibly motivated.

But something different happens.

You repeat those behaviours often enough that eventually they stop feeling like decisions.

Training becomes something you do.

Preparing your food becomes normal.

Going to bed because you’re training early becomes part of your routine.

There’s less negotiating,
